explanation.description: Example Markdown. Use $...$ for math and backticks for code, array access, and property access. Put example-specific diagrams and fenced code here.

statementMarkdown.description: Problem Markdown. Use $...$ for formulas, Big O, numbers, arithmetic, comparisons, and mathematical variables such as n. Use backticks for code identifiers, indexing, and property access such as nums[i] and nums.length, even inside a formula. Example: $1 \le$ `nums[i]` $\le 50$. Use language-tagged fenced blocks for multiline code or pseudocode and $$ on separate lines for display math.

hiddenCaseCounts.description: Number of hidden cases by stage. Stage 0 is the base suite.

recommendationReason.description: Practice ranking explanation; contains no other player history.

canCancel.description: False when the viewer can read the submission but does not own it.

submissionDeadline.description: Earlier shared cutoff when every remaining competitor has settled time penalties.

FilterMatch.description: Match any selected value by default, or require all selected values.

path.description: Walk into each element or a zero-based index before measuring. For example, ["each"] with length measures each row; ["each", 0] with value selects the first column.

offset.description: Add this integer to each numeric measurement, for bounds such as n - 1.

total.description: Sum all projected numeric measurements into one number, such as the total length of all rows.

operations.description: Apply numeric operations in order after measuring, totaling, and adding the offset. Sequences combine at matching positions; scalars broadcast.

minInclusive.description: Include the lower bound. Omitted is inclusive; false is strict.

maxInclusive.description: Include the upper bound. Omitted is inclusive; false is strict.

quantifier.description: all (default): every projected value/pair satisfies the rule; any: at least one does. Empty projections satisfy all and fail any.

pairing.description: Compare matching positions and require equal projection sizes. Omitted compares all combinations.

direction.description: Ordering direction. Omitted is asc. Applies only to ordering properties.

negated.description: When true, exclude every listed value. Omitted allows only listed values.

name.description: A name used in the statement for a derived input measurement.

text.description: Use only for rules without a structured equivalent. Use Markdown with LaTeX for math and backticks for program accesses.
